solutionDepth.title: A closer look at the work.

one.title: Diagnosis and financial objectives
one.body: Examine liquidity, maturities, cost, amortization, collateral, covenants and funding concentration. Relate the current structure to what the company wants to do: grow, acquire, refinance or preserve flexibility.
one.value: A recommendation guided by the business, not just the available credit product.

two.title: Business plan and capital needs
two.body: Review management's plan or develop projections from operating drivers. Connect revenue, margin, working capital, capex, earnings, the balance sheet and cash. Distinguish targets, contracted data and assumptions under discussion.
two.value: Understand how much capital is needed, when and under which assumptions.

three.title: Structuring alternatives
three.body: Discuss instruments, sources and uses, tranches, tenors, amortization, collateral and conditions. Compare cost, risk, flexibility and dependencies, including the effect of debt service on cash.
three.value: Compare economically developed structures with clear criteria for choosing.

four.title: Economic viability and market reality
four.body: Separate three questions: does the structure fit the business, does it make economic sense, and is there appetite on the intended terms? Historical references require a date and context; they are not current quotes.
four.value: Know what the analysis supports and what still needs market confirmation.

one.title: Documents, research and reconciliation
one.body: Organize incoming information, seek evidence, compare sources and surface discrepancies. Reported numbers, proposed adjustments and analytical assumptions must remain distinguishable.
one.value: Reduce the work of rebuilding the baseline before the analysis can begin.

two.title: Model building and review
two.body: Develop operating projections, cash flows, debt schedules, sources and uses. In a review, examine links, formulas, hardcodes, circularities, balances and conventions. The horizon and frequency should follow the decision.
two.value: Discuss the model and its limitations, beyond receiving a spreadsheet.

three.title: Scenarios and testing the limits
three.body: Preserve management's case and identify the analytical baseline. Explore downside, sensitivities, stress and cash or covenant thresholds according to the question. Discuss assumptions before execution.
three.value: Understand which factors change the recommendation and why.

four.title: Storyline, models and materials
four.body: Define the decision and audience before drafting. A board, committee, client and lender call for different messages: presentation, credit memo, teaser, info pack or indicative term sheet. Institutional templates and coordinated updates should be verified within the adoption scope.
four.value: Bring the analysis into the meeting and continue the discussion with reviewable materials.

one.title: Capital knowledge with context
one.body: An institution, manager, vehicle, program and team are not the same thing. Instruments, ticket sizes, tenors, collateral, exclusions and decision processes need context and current information. Declared interest, a completed transaction and present capacity are different evidence.
one.value: Avoid treating a directory of institutions as a set of confirmed mandates.

two.title: Fit with criteria and rationale
two.body: Compare the transaction with the mandate, starting with material restrictions. Separate compatibility, conditions to confirm and disqualifiers. Unknown information remains unknown; it should not artificially improve the assessment of fit.
two.value: Prioritize investigation and outreach with understandable reasons.

three.title: Preparation and authorized sharing
three.body: Organize the rationale, terms and package for the intended recipient. The choice of counterparties and what to share remains with the user. The investor's or company's internal assessment retains its own context.
three.value: Prepare a qualified conversation while retaining control over information.

four.title: Market knowledge applied to structuring
four.body: Allocator relationships have a role in the product: understanding what each institution evaluates and translating that knowledge into structuring, materials and qualification. Appetite and terms need reconfirmation at the time of approach.
four.value: Incorporate financing criteria before presenting the transaction to the market.

The difference is in the method.
Not the luck of the prompt.
method.intro: Investment banking, DCM and corporate finance experience applied to the questions, the calculations and the way the work gets done.
method.photoAlt: A workstation with a financial model and term sheet on the left monitor and the Offroad interface on the right.
method.modelsBody: Frontier models support reading, extraction, research and drafting. Financial specialization directs how those capabilities are used.
method.expertiseBody: Business context, the user's role, the instrument and institutional criteria determine what to investigate and how to interpret it.

workflow.title: Specialized workflows
workflow.body: Intent defines the work: what to examine, in which order, against which criteria and when the evidence is sufficient to proceed. A credit assessment does not follow the same logic as a client approach.

calculations.title: Deterministic financial logic
calculations.body: Financial calculations follow formalized rules outside text generation. Identical inputs and methodology produce identical results. Definitions of debt, EBITDA, coverage and debt service must be explicit, not assumed.

materials.title: Materials built for the decision-maker
materials.body: A board, a credit committee and a lender need different messages. The analysis supports the rationale; the audience determines the structure, the level of detail and the questions the materials must answer.

detail.title: The detail that changes the conclusion
detail.body: Recurring adjustments, contractual definitions, revenue concentration, amortization and collateral can change the case. These details guide the investigation instead of relying on the user to remember the right question.

market.label: Capital intelligence
market.title:
A structure must make sense
to the capital behind it.
market.intro: Understanding how capital is evaluated improves transaction design, preparation and the choice of counterparties.
market.leftTitle: Prepare the case for real scrutiny.
market.leftBody: Frame the capital need, anticipate credit questions and present the rationale in the way the market evaluates a transaction.
market.rightBody: Compare the opportunity with mandate criteria before committing the team to reconciling documents and deepening the analysis.
market.criteriaTitle: Transaction and mandate, assessed against the same criteria
market.relationshipTitle: Market knowledge feeds back into the analysis.
market.relationshipBody: Allocator relationships have a role in the product: understanding criteria and decision practices, then translating them into structuring, materials and qualification. Appetite and terms need confirmation at the time of approach.
market.note: Connection depends on fit, current information and permission to share. The credit decision remains with the lender.

journey.label: How it works
journey.title:
From scattered documents
to a funding-ready opportunity.
journey.intro: Start with a question or the documents you already have. Complete one task or develop the entire transaction, with guidance at every step.

start.label: Start
start.prompt: I want to finance our expansion. Where do we begin?
start.response: With the investment plan and when the business needs cash. We can begin with what you already have and identify the missing information together.
start.title: A question is already a starting point.
start.note: Documents are requested as the analysis needs them, with a reason for each request.

investigate.label: Investigate
investigate.prompt: Here are the P&L and debt schedule. What should we verify?
investigate.response: Let's reconcile the baseline, distinguish approved adjustments from hypotheses and compare debt with earnings. Historical leverage does not replace an assessment of future cash flow.
investigate.title: A basis for discussing capital.
investigate.note: Sources, adjustments and definitions need to travel with the numbers.

model.label: Model
model.prompt: Which assumptions would you change for a downside case, and why?
model.response: I would examine the ramp-up of new locations, margins and working capital needs. First we discuss the rationale and assumptions. The simulation follows your direction.
model.title: The scenario starts with the business.
model.note: You can adjust the proposal before calculating its effects on cash, coverage and liquidity.

prepare.label: Prepare
prepare.prompt: Turn the analysis into a board presentation and prepare the financing package.
prepare.response: The board needs to decide on the structure and constraints. The lender needs to understand the business, the credit and the terms. Both sets of materials share the analysis, but tell different stories.
prepare.title: The same analysis. The right message.
prepare.note: A board or client decision can direct the revision of the model, terms and materials.

connect.label: Connect
connect.prompt: Whom does it make sense to approach for this transaction?
connect.response: Let's assess the structure against capital criteria: instrument, ticket size, tenor, risk, collateral and restrictions. Each recommendation needs a fit rationale and points to confirm.
connect.title: A reasoned shortlist.
connect.note: This example does not represent a credit offer, a confirmed counterparty or a funding guarantee.

journey.modelOne: Time until a new location generates cash
journey.connectOne: Compare the transaction with the mandate
journey.connectTwo: Identify open questions before the approach
journey.connectThree: Decide what can leave the project
journey.continuityTitle: The conversation continues. So does the work.
journey.continuityBody: Challenge an assumption, explore another structure or return with a committee decision. Offroad is designed to carry the analysis forward, without restarting the reasoning with each request.

collaboration.body: Our product direction connects comments, reviews and approvals to sources and materials. Advanced collaboration and consolidation workflows should be validated in a demonstration against their implementation status.

security.body: The architecture uses organization-level access controls and private document storage. Identity, retention, provider and sharing requirements are addressed during institutional evaluation.

trust.status: Current controls and evolving capabilities are presented separately during platform evaluation.
trust.soc: SOC 2 Type II is an objective of our security program. We do not yet have a SOC 2 report.

offering.title:

The capacity to execute.

advisor.label: EXPERT ADVISOR
advisor.title: An experienced advisor to think it through.
advisor.benefit: Develop alternatives. Challenge the first answer.
advisor.body: The domain knowledge of a senior banker, an experienced CFO and a credit investor to discuss structures, challenge assumptions and recommend the next step.
advisor.detail: The conversation can begin before there is a defined answer. Offroad identifies what is missing, explains why it matters and focuses the analysis on what could change the decision.

analyst.label: HANDS-ON ANALYST
analyst.title: An analyst who does the whole job.
analyst.benefit: You set the direction. The work comes back ready to review.
analyst.body: Extracts, reconciles, models and prepares the materials. A source for every number, deterministic calculations and discrepancies surfaced before they become conclusions.
analyst.detail: Models, presentations, memoranda and debt schedules draw on the same baseline. Review assumptions and results, request changes and direct further work.

connection.label: QUALIFIED CONNECTION
connection.title: Reach the capital that takes this risk.
connection.benefit: Know who they are, what they invest in and why this deal fits.
connection.body: Market intelligence informs the structure from the start. Mandates, criteria and relevant transaction history explain fit and guide the approach.
connection.detail: The rationale shows what fits, what needs to change and what still requires confirmation. A strong score cannot override a mandate restriction or imply credit approval.

offering.principle: Think with someone who has sat on your side of the table. Execute with precision. Reach lenders who invest in your kind of risk.
offering.empowerBody: More depth in every analysis. More cases per professional. More time for the decision. Judgment, counterparty relationships and decisions remain with the people doing the work.

receivables.label: Receivables
receivables.question: We have BRL {receivables} million in receivables across multiple originators and debtors. What is the best way to fund working capital, and why?
receivables.response: I would start with the liquidity the portfolio can release and the risk the company retains. The instrument follows that assessment.
receivables.next: Compare a receivables-backed facility with a Brazilian FIDC structure, taking the portfolio constraints into account.

board.label: Board meeting
board.question: The board meets on Wednesday. I need alternatives to our current capital structure and what each changes in cost, maturity and risk.
board.response: I would bring comparable alternatives to the board, showing how each affects cash flow, debt maturities and financial flexibility.
board.next: Connect the current debt to business projections and make explicit what each alternative preserves or constrains.

pricing.label: Bank proposal
pricing.question: The bank proposed a CCB facility at CDI plus {spread}%. Is that market pricing for our credit profile?
pricing.response: The spread alone cannot answer that. We need transactions with comparable credit profiles, maturities and collateral, at the same reference date.
pricing.next: Review the complete proposal and find comparable references before concluding whether the pricing is appropriate.

analyst.direction: Prepare the model and materials for the board meeting.

analyst.deckDetail: The decision, alternatives and consequences organized for the board.

analyst.debtDetail: Lender, instrument, maturities, amortization, collateral and obligations reconciled.

companies.title: Build the capital plan you need to take to the board.
companies.benefit: Explore the options. Develop the model. Present your recommendation.

one.label: Understand the plan
one.prompt: We are expanding the store network. Before raising debt, I want to understand what we need to finance and take to the board.
one.reply: Let's separate new-store investment, expansion working capital and refinancing of existing debt. Is the opening schedule agreed? It determines when cash is needed and how long the financing must cover the ramp-up.
one.title: Three funding needs. Different structures.
one.note: Understand the uses of funds before discussing the structure.

two.label: Build the analysis
two.prompt: Use the P&L and debt schedule. I want a consistent baseline before discussing debt capacity.
two.reply: Adjusted EBITDA starts with reported earnings and approved adjustments. Historical leverage is a starting point, not a measure of expansion financing capacity. We need to assess debt service against available cash during the rollout.
two.title: A reconciled baseline for capital decisions.
two.detailTwo: Investment, working capital and debt service
two.note: Every figure tied to its source.

three.label: Prepare for the board
three.prompt: Prepare the board materials. Show the financing alternatives and make the outstanding decisions clear.
three.reply: The materials should cover the expansion plan, uses of funds and financing alternatives. I will distinguish approved assumptions from open decisions, including timing, collateral and minimum liquidity.
three.title: A structured board discussion.
three.detailTwo: Structure, tenor, collateral and cash impact
three.detailThree: Assumptions to approve and next steps
three.note: Board feedback informs the next version.

advisors.label: Advisors
advisors.title: Meet your client with a financing thesis, not a company summary.
advisors.benefit: From meeting preparation to the transaction model and materials.

one.label: Prepare the approach
one.prompt: I am meeting Rede Horizonte. I want to discuss its expansion and bring a financing hypothesis.
one.reply: I would start with the relationship between store openings and cash generation during ramp-up. The hypothesis is to separate investment financing from expansion working capital. We need to confirm timing and understand how existing collateral limits a new structure.
one.title: A hypothesis for the client discussion.
one.detailThree: Timing, cash flow and available collateral
one.note: The thesis guides the meeting. It does not replace the assessment.

two.label: Develop the thesis
two.prompt: Organize the numbers that support this discussion and highlight what we cannot conclude yet.
two.reply: The historical baseline supports a consistent discussion of earnings and debt. It does not yet support a financing amount: we still need the investment schedule, cash flow projections and available collateral.
two.title: Evidence behind the thesis. Gaps made explicit.
two.note: A commercial hypothesis is not an approved financing structure.

three.label: Develop the transaction
three.prompt: The client confirmed the priority. Organize the work on the model, term sheet and transaction materials.
three.reply: Let's incorporate the meeting feedback into the same project. The model should reflect the uses of funds and agreed assumptions; the term sheet should translate the structure; and the presentation should explain the company, transaction and credit rationale.
three.title: One rationale. Three consistent deliverables.
three.note: Client feedback updates the work without restarting the analysis.

investors.label: Investors
investors.title: Build your own underwriting. Do not inherit the originator's conclusion.
investors.benefit: Challenge assumptions, focus due diligence and prepare for investment committee.

one.label: Form a view
one.prompt: I received Rede Horizonte's teaser and model. What warrants diligence before we move forward?
one.reply: I would focus the first review on EBITDA quality, cash generation during expansion and structural protections. The analysis needs to distinguish documented evidence from assumptions made by the originator.
one.title: Three priorities for due diligence.
one.note: Mandate fit is necessary. It is not an underwriting conclusion.

two.label: Challenge assumptions
two.prompt: Before building a downside case, which assumptions would you change and why?
two.reply: I would test slower store ramp-up, higher working capital absorption and margin pressure. These factors can reduce cash available for debt service. Before calculating, we need to agree on the severity and duration of each stress.
two.title: A downside grounded in the business.
two.detailOne: Revenue takes longer to reach plan
two.detailTwo: Inventory and receivables absorb more cash
two.detailThree: Less cash generated per unit sold
two.note: Agree on the rationale first. Calculate when you ask.

three.label: Prepare for committee
three.prompt: Prepare a memo with our view, outstanding diligence and the conditions for continuing the assessment.
three.reply: The memo should distinguish the originator's thesis from our assessment. I will organize identified risks, available evidence, open diligence and protections to discuss. The investment decision remains with the committee.
three.title: Your credit view, documented.
three.detailOne: What supports the investment and what could change it
three.note: A memo for your decision. Not a retelling of the pitch.

solutions.title: Capital strategy, analysis and execution.

strategy.title: Develop the company's capital strategy.
strategy.intro: Connect the business plan to investment, working capital and existing debt. Explore structures that address each funding need.
strategy.pain: Growth, refinancing and liquidity protection may call for very different structures. Starting with a financial product can miss the question that actually needs answering.
strategy.oneBody: Connect the business plan to investment, working capital, debt maturities and available cash.
strategy.twoBody: Compare tenor, benchmark rates, amortization, collateral and restrictions. Identify what each structure solves and what it demands in return.
strategy.threeBody: Organize the recommendation, the conditions it depends on and the issues that need to be validated before proceeding.
strategy.output: A set of reasoned alternatives, explicit assumptions and a focused agenda for the decision.
strategy.example: The investment makes sense. Which financing structure lets us execute it without compromising liquidity?

execution.title: Develop models, term sheets and materials.
execution.intro: Prepare the financial model, transaction presentation or credit memo using the project's sources and assumptions.
execution.pain: Scattered information, inconsistent definitions and conflicting versions make execution harder. Sources, assumptions, conclusions and deliverables need to stay aligned.
execution.oneBody: Analyze company documents and data, identify gaps and distinguish reported information from adjustments and assumptions.
execution.twoBody: Develop projections, debt service and sensitivities using assumptions discussed with the team.
execution.threeBody: Structure models and materials for the audience: management, a client, a committee or a counterparty.
execution.output: Models, memos, presentations and transaction materials, as agreed within scope and subject to your review.
execution.example: An assumption changed. What needs to be revised in the model, the recommendation and the materials?

intelligence.title: Assess the fit between the transaction and the mandate.
intelligence.intro: Instrument, investment size, tenor, sector and collateral inform counterparty selection and opportunity assessment.
intelligence.pain: A contact list does not explain who could finance a transaction, on what terms or why an investor should pay attention.
intelligence.oneTitle: Understand the transaction and the mandate
intelligence.oneBody: Connect sector, company size, ticket, tenor, instrument, collateral and investment criteria.
intelligence.twoBody: Distinguish compatibility, constraints and missing information. Fit guides the analysis; it does not mean approval.
intelligence.threeBody: Define the rationale for the approach and what information may be shared with each counterparty, subject to authorization.
intelligence.output: A reasoned assessment of fit, qualification questions and materials appropriate to the approach.
intelligence.example: Who has a mandate for this structure, and what do they need to understand to assess it?

companies.title: From the business plan to the capital plan.
companies.intro: Discuss funding needs, prepare the board analysis and develop materials for conversations with the market.
companies.pain: A financing decision needs to serve the company's plan, not just the available offer. Tenor, cash flow, collateral and flexibility need to be assessed together.
companies.oneTitle: Translate the plan into a funding need
companies.oneBody: Connect investment, operations and working capital to cash flow and the debt profile.
companies.twoBody: Explore alternatives and their effects on liquidity, debt service, collateral and the ability to fund what comes next.
companies.threeBody: Develop the rationale and materials for the board and counterparties suited to the funding need.
companies.output: A foundation for deciding, defending the structure and negotiating with a clearer understanding of the alternatives.
companies.example: We want to expand. How much capital do we need, when and on what terms?

advisors.title: From the client thesis to transaction execution.
advisors.intro: Company research, meeting preparation, modeling and materials for investment banking, DCM and corporate finance teams.
advisors.pain: The quality of advice depends on analytical depth and the ability to execute at the pace of a transaction. Preparation needs to go beyond a company summary.
advisors.oneBody: Investigate the business, capital structure and events that justify an approach or recommendation.
advisors.twoBody: Explore structures, challenge assumptions and develop cash flow, risk and credit analysis within the mandate.
advisors.threeBody: Prepare models and materials aligned with the team's methods, the stage of the transaction and the audience.
advisors.output: More support for research, analysis and production, with judgment and relationships staying with the professionals.
advisors.example: We have a meeting tomorrow. What is the transaction hypothesis, and how do we support it?

investors.title: Credit analysis from your institution's perspective.
investors.intro: Assess the opportunity, challenge the originator's assumptions and prepare diligence and investment committee materials.
investors.pain: The originator's materials are a starting point. The decision requires an independent view of the company, risk, return and protection provided by the structure.
investors.oneTitle: Start with a mandate-led first look
investors.oneBody: Identify fit, constraints and issues worth investigating before committing the team's time.
investors.twoBody: Challenge assumptions, review cash generation, assess downside scenarios and make disagreements explicit.
investors.threeTitle: Set conditions and monitor the thesis
investors.threeBody: Organize terms, protections and questions for the committee. Reassess the position when performance or conditions change.
investors.output: An independent view to support diligence, committee review, negotiation and monitoring. The institution retains the decision.
investors.example: The opportunity fits the mandate. Does the risk make sense, and on what terms?

growth.title: Prepare the financing for expansion.
growth.intro: Investment, working capital and cash during ramp-up, in one capital plan.
growth.pain: The company wants to expand capacity. Investment is estimated, but working capital needs, implementation timing and the required cash cushion remain unclear.
growth.oneBody: Connect capacity expansion, revenue, margins, investment and working capital requirements.
growth.twoTitle: Locate the funding need in time
growth.twoBody: Examine periods of peak cash pressure and the impact of implementation delays.
growth.threeBody: Compare drawdowns, grace periods and amortization with expected cash generation and company constraints.
growth.output: Cash flow projections, an assessment of funding needs and alternatives for discussion with the board and lenders.
growth.example: How much do we need to raise to grow without running short of cash along the way?

terms.title: Compare proposals. Prepare the negotiation.
terms.intro: Term sheets, payment schedules, collateral and covenants assessed against the company's plan.
terms.pain: The decision needs to account for what each proposal enables. Organize tenor, drawdowns, amortization, collateral and obligations to understand the impact on cash and the capacity to fund the plan.
terms.oneBody: Put the offers on a consistent basis, including benchmark rates, charges, expenses and contractual obligations.
terms.twoBody: Model cash flows, debt service and relevant sensitivities before concluding on cost and repayment capacity.
terms.threeBody: Identify which terms would change the recommendation and which changes are worth discussing with each lender.
terms.output: A structured comparison, negotiation points and a decision rationale with explicit assumptions and limitations.
terms.example: We received two term sheets. Compare the terms and prepare the points we need to negotiate.

pitch.title: Prepare a thesis for the client meeting.
pitch.intro: An approach grounded in the business, company events and capital structure.
pitch.pain: A meeting with company management is coming up. The team needs to understand what changed in the business, where a financial need exists and why a transaction might make sense now.
pitch.oneBody: Review disclosures, strategy, investment, debt and developments relevant to the approach.
pitch.twoBody: Connect the identified need to structural alternatives and questions management needs to answer.
pitch.threeBody: Develop the briefing, question agenda and materials that present the thesis without treating assumptions as facts.
pitch.output: A company briefing, a transaction hypothesis and a presentation tailored to the meeting.
pitch.example: What do we have that is relevant to discuss with this company tomorrow?

credit.title: Develop the credit assessment.
credit.intro: Reconciled sources, cash generation, risks, mitigants and exceptions to institutional policy.
credit.pain: The documents have arrived. The analysis needs to distinguish reported performance from the cash generation that actually supports the debt, within the institution's criteria.
credit.oneBody: Reconcile sources, identify proposed adjustments and clarify material inconsistencies or gaps.
credit.twoBody: Analyze cash flow, leverage, coverage, structure and downside scenarios using the applicable methodology.
credit.threeBody: Set out risks, mitigants, conditions, policy exceptions and unresolved questions for the team's review.
credit.output: An analytical foundation and a supporting credit assessment. Credit approval is not delegated to the platform.
credit.example: What supports repayment capacity, and under what conditions is this structure acceptable?

investment.title: Build your own assessment of the opportunity.
investment.intro: An independent view to guide diligence and investment committee discussion.
investment.pain: The teaser appears to fit the mandate. Before proceeding, the team needs to understand which assumptions support the thesis and whether it agrees with them.
investment.oneBody: Compare the opportunity with instrument, sector, ticket, tenor, collateral and return criteria.
investment.twoBody: Challenge adjustments, rebuild key assumptions and examine downside cases without confusing the originator's thesis with the investor's.
investment.threeBody: Organize questions, additional document requests and the terms that could make the opportunity investable.
investment.output: A first look, diligence agenda and investment memo shaped by the institution's mandate and perspective.
investment.example: What do we need to confirm to build conviction in this opportunity?

monitoring.title: Reassess the credit. Prepare the waiver review.
monitoring.intro: Compare performance with the original thesis and assess the implications for cash, covenants and structural protection.
monitoring.pain: A company reported weaker-than-expected results or requested a waiver. The team needs to understand the effect on cash flow, obligations and protection of the position.
monitoring.oneBody: Compare reported performance with the previous analytical base and clarify the causes of the deviations.
monitoring.twoBody: Examine liquidity, debt service, covenants and assumptions about recovery or further deterioration.
monitoring.threeBody: Organize the rationale for monitoring, additional diligence, renegotiation or waiver review.
monitoring.output: Updated analysis, issues requiring attention and materials for the committee or responsible team's decision.
monitoring.example: Is the deviation temporary, or does it change the conditions under which we accepted the risk?

start.howTitleMuted: Offroad prepares the path to market.
start.howIntro: First, we want to understand the company: what it does, its sector and markets, its strengths and what sets it apart. Then, the project it intends to finance and the use of proceeds. In a few lines, in your own words. If an institutional presentation already exists, simply attach it.
start.howAnalysis: Share whatever is available: business plan, financial statements, contracts, accounting records or corporate documents. PDF, Excel or photo, exactly as they are. Offroad reads everything to understand how the company operates, its financial dynamics and the intended transaction. We reconcile sources so every statement has documentary support, flag discrepancies and identify points that require clarification. We also anticipate what investors will require, including for a preliminary assessment, so material issues do not surface only midway through the process.
start.howMarket: From there, we propose structures aligned with the transaction and prepare a complete information package, including a teaser, financial projections and an indicative term sheet, in the format the market expects. We understand financing products and maintain relationships with a broad base of capital providers. We know what each one reviews, how they review it and what they require for approval. This direction increases the transaction's probability of success. The introduction is conducted through the platform, with your authorization and only to investors whose mandates are aligned.
start.youDo1Body: What it does, its sector and markets, its strengths and differentiators. If you already have an institutional presentation, simply attach it.
start.youDo2Body: What you intend to finance and the amount you have in mind. In your own words, without a form.
start.youDo3Body: Financial statements, contracts and corporate documents. Drag and drop, in any format.
start.youDo4Body: An intuitive chat with our specialized AI, focused only on what the documents did not answer.

start.offroadDoes2Body: We reconcile sources so every piece of information has documentary support. If something is unclear, we ask.

MandateRegistry.title: Funds and mandates
MandateRegistry.intro: Register each fund and the mandate it runs today. The record enters as a draft; confirming it is a separate act, with a date and an origin.
MandateRegistry.boundary: A confirmed mandate inside its validity window is what a case reads as current interest. A public record and a past transaction stay research, never confirmed interest.
MandateRegistry.registerIntro: Pick a fund already registered, or give a name and a strategy to create one. Leave blank whatever the manager does not restrict.
MandateRegistry.empty: No fund registered yet. Until a mandate is confirmed, this manager appears as a verified candidate in no case at all.

errors.invalid: A field falls outside the mandate contract. Check the investment range, the tenor and the validity window.
errors.denied: Your organization does not manage mandates.
errors.not_found: This record is no longer available.
errors.conflict: The record was withdrawn and cannot be confirmed again.
errors.save: The change could not be saved.

fields.sources: Sources for this record (one per line)

channelHelp.direct_declaration: The manager declares the mandate here, signed in as itself. No document and no contact are attached.
channelHelp.official_document: Name the document the confirmation rests on, in words somebody else can check.
channelHelp.recorded_contact: Give the identifier of the recorded contact and the date it happened.

renewal.due_soon: The validity window is close to closing. Confirm again for the mandate to keep counting in the selection.
renewal.expired: The validity window has closed. This mandate left the selection until it is confirmed again.
renewal.unconfirmed: Not confirmed yet. While it is a draft, this fund does not enter the selection.

MandateRegistry.windowOpen: In force since {from}, with no end date.
MandateRegistry.withdrawnNote: A withdrawn mandate does not come back. Register a new version to describe the current mandate.
MandateRegistry.confirmIntro: A confirmation records who confirmed, when, and through which origin. It sends nothing outside and contacts nobody.
MandateRegistry.pendingBody: These funds exist in your registry and have no structured mandate yet. With no confirmed mandate they enter no case selection.
MandateRegistry.sourcesHelp: Where this mandate came from: a regulation, a minute, an email from the manager. A public record and a past transaction do not belong here.
